\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.ClassPSPACE.TQBFHardMachine}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Code length]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.codeLen}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.codeLen}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.W, Complexity.Codec.wP}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols, and let
$n,s\in\mathbb{N}$. Its code length at parameters $n,s$ is $W(N)(2s+1)+w_P(n)+1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial block condition]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.blockInit}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.blockInit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.initLang, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x,\beta$
be Boolean lists, and let $s,L\in\mathbb{N}$. The initial block condition holds when the
pair encoding of $x$ with the pair encoding of the first $L$ entries of $\beta$ and the
binary expansion of $s$ belongs to the initial language of $N$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Accepting block condition]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.blockAcc}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.blockAcc}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.acceptLang, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x,\beta$
be Boolean lists, and let $s,L\in\mathbb{N}$. The accepting block condition holds when
the pair encoding of $x$ with the pair encoding of the first $L$ entries of $\beta$ and
the binary expansion of $s$ belongs to the acceptance language of $N$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Block transition condition]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.blockStep}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.blockStep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.stepLang, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let
$x,\beta,\beta'$ be Boolean lists, and let $s,L\in\mathbb{N}$. The block transition
condition holds if either $\beta=\beta'$, or the pair encoding of $x$ with the pair
encoding of the first $L$ entries of $\beta$ and the pair encoding of the first $L$
entries of $\beta'$ and the binary expansion of $s$ belongs to the step language of $N$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of step counts]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.steps_mono}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.steps_mono}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TQBFHard.Steps}
\difficulty{4}
Let $w$ be a natural number and let $E$ be a relation on Boolean strings that is
reflexive, meaning $E(B,B)$ for every string $B$. If $k\le k'$, $B$ has length $w$, and
there is a $k$-step chain from $A$ to $B$, then there is a $k'$-step chain from $A$ to
$B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Step chains yield reachability]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.steps_reflTransGen}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.steps_reflTransGen}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.stepLang, Complexity.TQBFHard.Steps, Complexity.TQBFHard.blockStep, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet,
and let $x$ be a Boolean string and $s,L,w,k$ be natural numbers. Define
$E(\beta,\beta')$ to hold when either $\beta=\beta'$ or the encoding of $x$, the
length-$L$ prefixes of $\beta$ and $\beta'$, and the binary representation of $s$
belongs to the machine's one-step configuration language. If there is a $k$-step chain
from Boolean strings $A$ to $B$ using $E$ and width $w$, then the length-$L$ prefixes of
$A$ and $B$ are related by the reflexive transitive closure of the relation that encodes
$x$, the two strings, and the binary representation of $s$ as a one-step machine
transition.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Transferring encoded paths to the step relation]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.reflTransGen_stepRel}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.reflTransGen_stepRel}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.StepRel, Complexity.Codec.pairEncode_inj, Complexity.Codec.stepLang, Complexity.LogProg.bits_injective, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $x$ be
a bit string, and let $s,u\in\mathbb N$. Suppose a bit string $\gamma$ is reachable from
the binary expansion of $u$ by a finite sequence of zero or more edges, each edge
encoding a one-step transition of $N$ on input $x$ between configurations whose
work-tape heads and contents lie within the window of radius $s$. If $\gamma$ is the
binary expansion of some $c\in\mathbb N$, then $c$ is reachable from $u$ by zero or more
steps of the corresponding encoded configuration relation with input $x$ and window
radius $s$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Language Membership and Midpoint Chains]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.mem_iff_mid}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.mem_iff_mid}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.bits_cfgCode, Complexity.Codec.length_cfgWord, Complexity.Codec.mem_acceptLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_iff_codeChain, Complexity.Codec.mem_initLang, Complexity.Codec.mem_of_codePath, Complexity.Codec.mem_stepLang, Complexity.Codec.pairEncode_inj, Complexity.LogProg.bits_injective, Complexity.TQBFHard.Mid, Complexity.TQBFHard.Steps, Complexity.TQBFHard.blockAcc, Complexity.TQBFHard.blockInit, Complexity.TQBFHard.blockStep, Complexity.TQBFHard.codeLen, Complexity.TQBFHard.mid_iff_steps, Complexity.TQBFHard.reflTransGen_stepRel, Complexity.TQBFHard.steps_mono, Complexity.TQBFHard.steps_reflTransGen, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.configBound}
\difficulty{6}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $L$
be a language of Boolean strings, and let $sp:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for
every input string $y$ there is a time $T$ such that every choice string of length $T$
makes $N$ halt, uses at most $sp(|y|)$ work-tape cells, and $y\in L$ exactly when some
such choice string makes $N$ halt with output $[\mathrm{true}]$. For any Boolean string
$x$ and natural numbers $s,w$ satisfying $sp(|x|)\le s$, $\mathrm{codeLen}(N,|x|,s)\le
w$, and $\mathrm{configBound}(|x|,s)\le 2^w$, membership $x\in L$ is equivalent to the
existence of length-$w$ bit strings $A,B$ such that the initial configuration of $N$ on
$x$ is encoded by the first $\mathrm{codeLen}(N,|x|,s)$ bits of $A$, $B$ encodes a
halting configuration with output $[\mathrm{true}]$, and $A$ and $B$ are related by $w$
levels of midpoint subdivision using the relation that holds when two strings agree or
encode a single machine step within the space window $s$.
\end{theorem}
